missionPremise: Operator ruling 2026-08-19 (OPS-16 A-019): two stores holding one subject is a by-product of an evolving product, so the answer is a statewide reconciliation PROGRAMME rather than a per-case adjudication. Same shape as A-002, which ruled that mud is a special-district TYPE and not its own rail. Case one is parcel 48021:36521, AO on node-facets:tier2 and AE on the flood-hazard-fact atom. Source: P:/doc_repo/_dispatches/2026-08-19_ss-w11_dispatch.md. Case one was VERIFIED at source by this lane before any work began; the magnitudes behind it were RELAYED from SS-W5 and were re-derived independently before being reported.
completionPredicate: A stranger can run one command per county and get (a) the full list of subjects held in more than one store, derived from the stores rather than hand-declared, (b) for each duplicate pair a per-entity classification into agree / one-sided / explained-by-sampling-point / split-subject / edition-differs / vintage-undecidable / genuine-conflict, each with its own denominator printed beside it, and (c) a named loser per pair with the evidence that makes retiring it safe. MET for the flood-zone subject in the two counties the dispatch names. NOT MET for the other seven subjects and the other eight tier2 counties, which are inventoried but unmeasured — stated plainly rather than narrated as complete.
scopeBasis: The dispatch names the detector as the first deliverable and flood as case one, not the case list, so scope is every store-pair in the spine holding the same subject for the same entity, measured where both stores actually hold data. Deliberately EXCLUDED and named so the omission reads as deliberate: writing any fix to either store (this lane is read-only and a retirement is an operator ruling per DEV_PROCESS 5.4); the SERVED layer (SS-W5 established under P-43 that the tier2 overlay reaches no browser, and re-probing would duplicate that lane); atom families with no second store, each listed with its reason in OUT_OF_SCOPE_STORES.

duplicateSubjectInventory.derivedFrom: 21 atom entity_types (loose index scan over atoms_entity_type_idx) + 22 place_layer_snapshots adapter_keys + information_schema columns for the cortex raw parcel tables
duplicateSubjectInventory.membershipRule: A store counts as a second home for a subject when it is keyed on the SAME ENTITY. A raw geo table whose rows are zone polygons, well bores or building footprints is an UPSTREAM of a parcel-keyed fact, not a duplicate of it — which is why tx_fema_nfhl_flood_zone is this programme's ground truth rather than one of its cases. txgio_parcel IS parcel-keyed, so its columns are genuine second homes.

verdictOnThePlannerPrediction.predicted: Bastrop's 8.69 percent is mostly staleness and collapses on refresh; Travis's 0.04 percent is mostly split parcels.
verdictOnThePlannerPrediction.verdict: FALSIFIED IN BOTH HALVES, and the premise beneath it does not survive its own denominators.
verdictOnThePlannerPrediction.detail: Staleness accounts for 0 of 5,424 Bastrop disagreements, so a refresh moves nothing. Split parcels account for 0 of 332 Travis disagreements; all 42 splits found anywhere are in Bastrop. And the 200x Bastrop/Travis contrast the vintage thesis was built on is 0.70 percentage points once each rate is taken over the population where a disagreement is arithmetically possible.
verdictOnThePlannerPrediction.preRegistration: CP1 pre-registered, before any county ran, that the two counties would land within a few points of each other and that the tile-sampling artifact would dominate in both. The result is inside that band. The classifier's firing tests were written before the first county ran.
verdictOnThePlannerPrediction.whatTheCauseActuallyIs: The tier2 bake quantises each parcel centroid to a 0.005-degree tile, issues ONE live FEMA ArcGIS point query at the tile CENTRE, and reuses that answer for every parcel in the tile. tier2 is not a worse answer to the same question; it is an answer to a different question — the flood zone of a point up to 366 m away.

retirementRecommendations.subject: flood-zone
retirementRecommendations.basis: Ground truth matches the atom in 5,714 of 5,714 non-split adjudicated cases and tier2 in zero. tier2 is coarser BY CONSTRUCTION (one FEMA query per 0.005-degree tile) and cannot be improved without abandoning the tiling that makes it affordable, so this is not a defect to fix. It also covers only 10 counties and 608,414 parcels against the atom's statewide coverage, and 84.97 percent of its Travis rows never fetched FEMA at all.
retirementRecommendations.consumerThatBreaks: NONE SERVING TODAY. That the overlay reaches no browser is RELAYED from SS-W5 under P-43 (mergeBakedBaseFacts never copies tier2 across) and was not re-probed by this lane. The three code readers WERE verified at source by this lane, in hauska-map at d3510a6: apps/property-explorer/src/workbench/tools/compare-facts.ts:200-201 exports floodCell(tier2) reading rec(rec(tier2)?.flood); apps/property-explorer/src/browse/brief-verdict.ts:94-105 reads sectionData(payload,'flood') then flood.floodZone; apps/property-explorer/src/share/share-verdict.ts:47-50 reads byId.get('flood') then flood.floodZone. All three must be repointed at the atom in the same change, or they render 'flood not verified here' permanently instead of accidentally. Note the shapes differ: the tier2 facet carries status / floodZone / zoneSubtype / provenance, while the atom carries floodZone / zoneSubtype / inSpecialFloodHazardArea / sourceVintage and no status field, so the repoint needs an adapter and is not a field rename.
retirementRecommendations.sequencing: Repoint the readers at the atom FIRST, then retire the store. Doing it in the other order converts an invisible defect into a visible regression.
retirementRecommendations.doNotDo: Do not 'reconcile and sync' the two stores. A sync leaves both maintained and they diverge again on the next bake — and here a sync would be worse than useless, because it would copy a 366-m-resolution answer over a parcel-resolution one.

retirementRecommendations.subject: flood-zone, second store
retirementRecommendations.basis: A per-engagement live-adapter cache with no refresh path, superseded by the bulk table it duplicates. No measurement needed at 176 rows.

retirementRecommendations.subject: buildable-envelope-status
retirementRecommendations.recommendation: RETIRE pls:node-facets:tier1#envelope and pls:node-facets:tier2#envelope. Keep atoms:buildable-envelope.
retirementRecommendations.basis: tier1's envelope was ALREADY retired in place — its payload carries declineReason atom_path_pending and the disclosure 'Tier-1 bake no longer authors product envelope confidence (anti-zombie). Read buildable-envelope from the property atom chain' — and it still answers. A store that has been told it is retired and still returns a value on every read is the worst of the three shapes, because nothing about the response reads as retired to a consumer. tier2's envelope is gated off by default and declines with a different reason for the same parcel.
retirementRecommendations.consumerThatBreaks: unmeasured; this subject has no measurement pass yet

retirementRecommendations.subject: zoning-district, land-use-code
retirementRecommendations.recommendation: DO NOT RETIRE YET. Measure first, then retire the COPY.
retirementRecommendations.basis: These are Class B copy/transform, not independent derivations: 52,700 of 62,260 Bastrop zoning-fact atoms carry sourceAdapter cortex-tier1-snapshot-breadth-bake and their own citation says 'breadth bake is TRANSFORM only'. A copy cannot diverge by method, only by refresh lag, so the divergence rate is a direct measure of lag — and tier1 was re-baked 2026-08-06 while those atoms were stamped 2026-08-04. Retiring the wrong side here would delete the 9,560 atoms that ARE independent city-GIS stamps.
retirementRecommendations.sequencing: Run the measurement pass, split the atom population by sourceAdapter, then retire only the transform half.

retirementRecommendations.subject: parcel-existence
retirementRecommendations.recommendation: DO NOT RETIRE. FIX. tier1 needs a retirement path.
retirementRecommendations.basis: This is the one case where the answer is not retirement. atoms:parcel-node carries a lifecycle and writes a positive retirement with its basis; tier1 has no lifecycle at all, so a parcel the source no longer publishes keeps its baked row and keeps serving. 48021:36521 is exactly this: parcel-node retired 2026-08-11, tier1 row still live and still carrying apn, acreage, land use and zoning. Retiring tier1 wholesale would take the working facts with it; the missing piece is a retirement propagation, not a deletion.

retirementRecommendations.subject: assessed-value, owner-name caches
retirementRecommendations.recommendation: DELETE pls:cad:tax and pls:cad:property (145 rows each, 42 non-empty each).
retirementRecommendations.basis: Per-engagement caches with no refresh path, carrying dollar figures and owner names that the appraisal-roll atom covers at roughly 5 M scale. A stale cache carrying a DOLLAR FIGURE is the one a customer is most likely to quote back at us.

retirementRecommendations.subject: extinguished-source caches
retirementRecommendations.recommendation: DELETE all cotality:* and regrid:* adapter rows. 22 rows carry values, 137 are empty objects, 159 rows total.
retirementRecommendations.basis: Cotality and Regrid are both EXTINGUISHED. Nothing refreshes these and nothing should. This is not a reconciliation case; it is a delete ruling, which is the operator's to make.

retirementRecommendations.subject: permits
retirementRecommendations.basis: The 6 non-empty rows match on a normalised street line and say so in their own caveat ('Not a parcel-id join'). The durable permit store is permit_record at 2,849,138 rows keyed on permit_number.

retirementRecommendations.subject: programme-level
retirementRecommendations.recommendation: ADD A SAMPLING CONTRACT TO THE ATOM RECORD, and make a source EDITION mandatory on any store that claims an external authority.
retirementRecommendations.basis: The two defects that made this case hard are both absences in the record, not disagreements in the data. The atom does not record the POINT it evaluated, so this lane had to reconstruct it from a second store. The tier2 record carries a bake timestamp where an edition belongs, so staleness is untestable from the record — the dispatch's own vintage-versus-split fork was undecidable on that side. Two stores that both name their sample geometry and their source edition can be reconciled by reading them; these two could not.

freeFindings.text: pnpm-lock.yaml on main omits postgres under packages/retrieval although packages/retrieval/package.json has declared postgres@^3.4.5 since PR #347, so pnpm install --frozen-lockfile FAILS on a clean checkout of main. CI never noticed: both workflows pass --frozen-lockfile=false. The one-line sync is in this branch. The guardrail question — a lockfile that is advisory is not a lockfile — is a backlog item and not this lane's to rule on.

Three concurrent full-table count(*) scans over atoms (entity_type='parcel-node', filtering on body->>'countyFips') were running from another session in parallel with each other during this lane's inventory pass. AGENT_CONTRACT section 4 permits at most ONE heavy scan at a time across all lanes on a shared database. Observed at pg_stat_activity pids 2339/2340/2341, identical query text and identical query_start. Reported and not acted on: killing another lane's work is destructive and not this lane's call.

A duplicate subject can live INSIDE one record, which this detector's shape cannot see. The setback-rule atom for 48021:36521 carries displayMeta.secondSource stating that the city's GIS layer 83 specifies corner side 10 for district GC while the atom's own layer-23 reading says 5, with the note 'the two city schedules conflict — verify which is in effect with the city'. One store, two values, an unresolved conflict shipped as a display note. Named in the registry's exclusion list so it reads as deliberate.

Six place_layer_snapshots adapters are 100 percent empty objects (cotality:zoning 65/65, cotality:parcels 54/54, cotality:rent-avm 12/12, cotality:propensity 12/12, regrid:parcels 2/2, regrid:zoning 2/2). An adapter key that exists and holds nothing reads as coverage to anything that enumerates keys — which is precisely the mistake this lane made at CP1 and had to correct.

Eleven Bastrop parcels where the atom matches ground truth at every point tested, the parcel lies wholly in one zone, and tier2 is simply wrong. Five of the eleven are near-consecutive prop ids (8727948, 8727992, 8727993, 8727994, 8727996), which suggests one bad FEMA tile rather than eleven independent errors. Untested.

whatRemainsOpen: 8 of the 10 tier2 counties are unmeasured for flood-zone: 48209, 48309, 48091, 48187, 48029, 48027, 48055, 48491, holding 516,573 tier2 rows. The MECHANISM is statewide because it lives in the bake rather than in the geography, but the RATE reported here is a two-county rate and must not be quoted as a statewide one.

7 of the 8 registered duplicate subjects have no measurement pass. The runner refuses them with an explicit error rather than returning zero, which is the honest failure mode, but inventoried is not measured.
The retirement recommendations are PROPOSALS. Retirements and deletions are operator rulings per DEV_PROCESS 5.4 and nothing was retired, deleted or deployed by this lane.
PR #349 is OPEN and unmerged by the dispatch's hard rule. Its CI conclusion string is reported to the planner separately.

The programme-level recommendation — a mandatory sampling contract on the atom record and a mandatory source edition on any store claiming an external authority — is the durable fix and is not implemented here.
